title: ATLAS boosted decision trees enable first observation of triple-W boson production
summary: In 139 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV LHC data, ATLAS observed simultaneous WWW production at 8.0σ (5.4σ expected) and measured an inclusive cross-section of 820 ± 100(stat) ± 80(syst) fb. The analysis selected same-sign dilepton-plus-jets and trilepton final states. Two boosted decision trees—one per channel—improved signal/background separation and supplied distributions for the fit. The measured rate is about 2.6σ above the Standard Model prediction, not a significant discrepancy.
ai_technology: Two boosted decision tree classifiers for the dilepton and trilepton channels

evidence.tested: In 139 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV LHC data, ATLAS observed simultaneous WWW production at 8.0σ (5.4σ expected) and measured an inclusive cross-section of 820 ± 100(stat) ± 80(syst) fb.
evidence.unknown: The final peer-reviewed paper reports 8.0σ (5.4σ expected), superseding the earlier 2021 conference-note/press account that quoted 8.2σ and 850 fb. CMS had previously observed combined inclusive production of three massive gauge bosons; this ATLAS paper is the first observation specifically of WWW production. The measured cross-section is about 2.6σ above the theory prediction, below a significant deviation, with data-driven background and systematic uncertainties included.
evidence.ai_role: The BDTs were trained separately for the two- and three-lepton channels, using 12 and 11 well-modelled event variables respectively, to discriminate WWW signal from background. Their output distributions entered the likelihood fit; the paper says the improved separation helped enable the observation.
